 Kiffin says he won’t complain about the LSU roster Brian Kelly left him. His assistants have. 
 By JON BLAU | Staff writer 
 Jon Blau

 Lane Kiffin doesn’t want to complain about the LSU roster Brian Kelly handed him, but he says his assistant coaches have.
 “I say, ‘Guess what? If they did a better job, we wouldn't be here,’” Kiffin said during a Sunday teleconference with reporters, a day after a 22-21 loss to Texas that eliminated the Tigers from the College Football Playoff discussion.
 The disappointment of that loss has stirred up a debate about how quickly Kiffin should have been able to revamp LSU’s roster with the availability of transfer talent and a rumored $50 million invested into athlete pay.
 As Kiffin sat with a 6-4 record, he was questioned Sunday about his plans for the future and his continued confidence in them.
 “I feel horrible for our fans, for our players, especially our older players. I hate that it ended the way it did yesterday. There's not one second (of doubt) about the plan for the future not working,” Kiffin said. “I can't comment on what a recruit that was just in here said. But no, I'm not worried about that at all.”
 He doesn’t believe momentum has been lost, and he continues to believe that LSU will always have better rosters than the one he’s currently managing.
 While the Tigers added 40-plus transfers this past offseason, Kiffin pointed to the fact that LSU had just two scholarship players who spent their entire careers in Baton Rouge and participated in Senior Day festivities this past weekend.
 Failures by the Kelly regime in high school recruiting and development, in Kiffin’s eyes, depleted the Tigers’ depth.
 “You may have premier players, which is what we have,” Kiffin said. “In order to build (depth), you need a couple classes … so it takes a little bit of time to do that. But again, you still should win these games.
 “The frustration is we should still be winning these games. Then as we get the deeper rosters, then hopefully instead of these games being right down to the wire, you win them by two scores.”
 Kiffin said the “middle to bottom” of LSU’s roster was so different in speed and length than Texas’ squad that he noticed as much pregame.
 And told his coaches that.
 “Hey, we got to coach really good today, win this game,” Kiffin said, “and then let's go fix the middle bottom of the roster, so they look like that one I just saw warm up.”
 LSU did not win. Texas running back Raleek Brown swung out into the flat, wide open, for a game-winning toss from Arch Manning.
 “I'm not being critical of players. I just watch our warmups,” Kiffin added. “You'll see a very big difference between what our backups look like and the teams we played the last two weeks.”
 Kiffin said he is not “trying to buy time” by bringing up the Tigers’ depth issues, which he said has resulted in the LSU defense rotating less than he would like.
 He said he hates to lose, but Kiffin isn’t sure LSU’s recruiting targets were overly affected by the Alabama and Texas losses because when they’re arriving is “not right now.”
 “They see the environment, they see the intensity, they see the stadium,” Kiffin said, “and they see how close the team is to being great, that you're playing top-10 teams, and you're ahead of both of them in the second half.
 “That's no concern at all, as soon as this portal starts.”
 Kiffin then launched into another defense of his move to have celebrities walk with the Tigers into the stadium for home games, as well as the basketball hoop on the sideline that players dunk on after scoring touchdowns.
 He knows some LSU fans don’t like it. But he recalled one recruit who was excited he got to meet social media personality Alix Earle and musician Shaboozey at the game.
 “All that stuff goes into that part of recruiting and building and how you put together great classes,” Kiffin said. “I know it's not everybody's favorite thing, but there's a reason for all of it.”
 The reason is LSU needs to recruit better.
 “I don't think I'm saying a secret, truth be told, of not really good recruiting,” Kiffin said of the Kelly era. “I'm not throwing a shot. I'm seeing not really good recruiting that got here and developed, or you wouldn't be in this situation or we wouldn't be here, too.”
